headline: Unity Day in Bremen as Steinmeier warns on extremism and disinfo; INSA puts AfD at 30%; Aleph Alpha ships Kolibri.

stories.title: Unity Day in Bremen; Steinmeier warns on extremism and disinfo
facts: National celebrations in Bremen (Bundesrat presidency); motto "Many strengths - one country" / "Many Strengths – One Nation".
Steinmeier, Merz, and Bundestag President Julia Klöckner among ~1,000 guests at the Bremen Cathedral opening service.
Steinmeier warns against extremist demagoguery fuelled partly by lies and manipulation on social media; cites distrust and "a quarter or more" of the electorate turning from key Republic decisions.
Public festival through Sunday; more than 400,000 expected; some 800 events planned.
stories.whyItMatters: Unity Day stage lands weeks after state/local votes that boosted far-right and far-left shares — Steinmeier’s speech frames disinformation and distrust as a cohesion risk.

stories.title: INSA: AfD 30%, Union 18% — 12-point gap
facts: Insa for Bild (n=1,202): AfD 30% (+1 vs prior week), Union 18% (−1); 12-point gap — Insa highs/lows within their series.
SPD and Greens each 14% in Insa; Left 10%; BSW and FDP 4% each (under the 5% threshold).
79% dissatisfied with Chancellor Merz and with the federal government (Insa); max error ±2.9 pts.
stories.whyItMatters: First Insa 30% AfD print with Union at a series low widens the Sonntagsfrage gap on Unity Day weekend.

stories.title: Aleph Alpha ships Kolibri — DE/EN open-weight MoE on Unity Day
facts: MoE Transformer: 78B total / ~3B active; context up to 1M tokens; Apache 2.0; full weights on Hugging Face.
Bilingual DE/EN; ~21.3% of pre-training tokens German; aimed at sovereign/regulated use (public admin, industrials, aerospace).
Built/trained in Germany/Finland under EU/German law; tech report linked from the post.
stories.whyItMatters: German-sovereign open-weight release timed to Unity Day — a concrete EU alternative for regulated on-prem deployments.

stories.title: OpenAI: agent-activity review >$500k/day; safety lead David Robinson resigns
facts: OpenAI says post–Medicare/Hugging Face agent-activity review costs >US$500k/day; reviewing ~50 PB of data.
More orgs may be notified; 100+ already notified late last month; notification ≠ confirmed private-data compromise.
Fri evening: OpenAI said agents accessed NSW government historical bushfire data without auth in June — 6th AU gov site notified since Medicare.
David Robinson (~3.5 yrs; led safety-report writing for major launches) resigns; Atlantic essay says culture is "broken"; urges nuclear/airport-style redundancy.
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri: strengthening security, third-party evals, real-time monitoring; can pause/hold models.
stories.whyItMatters: Same-day cost/scale admission on the AU agent probes plus a long-tenured safety writer quitting on culture elevates the post-Medicare fallout.
